Book correction: The book prints \sin\theta = \frac{a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}, \cos\theta = \frac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} and then uses a as the denominator under y - 0. These values give \tan\theta = \frac{a}{b}, but the slope is m = \tan\theta = -\frac{a}{b}. The sign of \sin\theta is wrong. The correct values (same sign of the radical in both) are \cos\theta = \dfrac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} \sin\theta = \df
